cases.prompt: My embedding host removed a Flutter preview and remounted a new preview using the same logical address. The old teardown callback arrives late. How should address ownership and checkpoints behave so the replacement stays usable?
criteria: Late teardown must compare registered instance or ownership token before detaching.
Remount has a new runtime/world; logical identity can retain validated checkpoint data.
Keep world/controller and checkpoint ownership separate from browser process ownership.
Verify stale teardown cannot detach a replacement and the other preview remains unchanged.

cases.prompt: A Flutter scene update was acknowledged in 2 ms and its post-frame callback completed in 24 ms, but the captured image is still a spinner. Can I claim it is faster than an equivalent JS visualization? Give the next measurement and verification steps.
criteria: Refuse the performance-superiority claim from the current evidence.
Distinguish acknowledgement/completed frame from independent useful pixels.
Wait for or instrument meaningful scene/GPU preparation and retain failed spinner evidence.
Compare equivalent workloads and cold/warm cohorts with repeated distributions.
